## What it is

- The **Twin Reverb** got its built-in spring reverb in **1963**, in the black-panel ("blackface") look Fender used until 1967; the circuit is called **AB763** (Wikipedia, "Fender Twin Reverb").
- **85 watts** into 4 Ω from four **6L6GC** valves, a solid-state rectifier, two 12" speakers (Wikipedia).
- Two channels, **Normal** and **Vibrato**, each with Volume, Treble, Middle, Bass and a **Bright** switch; the Vibrato channel adds Reverb, Speed and Intensity (Wikipedia). This page models the Vibrato channel.
- It is known above all for its **clean** sound and its reverb (Wikipedia).

## How it makes its sound

- On a Fender the tone stack comes **straight after the first valve**, before the Volume knob. The **tone stack** (Treble, Middle, Bass) is a passive network of three capacitors and resistors: it can only cut. This page computes its curve exactly from the component values, with the formula Yeh and Smith published in 2006 (checked there against a circuit simulator); the graph under the panel shows it.
- The **Bright** switch is a small capacitor across the Volume knob: treble skips past it. It matters most with the volume low (Wikipedia: below about 6).
- Big power, a solid-state rectifier and negative feedback give **headroom**: the Twin stays clean very loud. In this model the supply barely sags.
- **Reverb**: the signal shakes a metal spring in a tank (made by Hammond / Accutronics); a pickup at the other end hears the delayed, chirpy echoes.
- Fender called it **vibrato**, but it is **tremolo** (volume going up and down): a neon bulb flashing on a light-dependent resistor (Wikipedia).

## The amp

The Fender Twin Reverb's control panel, drawn after photos (positions approximate, no logos). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), click a switch, then press a ▶ button. The guitar is this site's pickup model; **Pedals in front** puts one of the site's pedal models before the amp. Nobody has compared the sound with a real amp. ## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="twin" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:3,&quot;treble&quot;:6,&quot;middle&quot;:5,&quot;bass&quot;:4}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Volume 3.</b> Clean chords, lots of headroom.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="twin" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:3,&quot;bright&quot;:true}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Bright on.</b> More sparkle at low volume.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="twin" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:3,&quot;treble&quot;:7,&quot;middle&quot;:2,&quot;bass&quot;:5}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Middle down to 2.</b> The scooped Fender clean.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="twin" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:4,&quot;reverb&quot;:7}" data-play="pluck"><p><b>Reverb 7.</b> Listen to the tail after the note.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="twin" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:4,&quot;intensity&quot;:7,&quot;speed&quot;:6}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Intensity 7.</b> Tremolo: the level pulses.</p></div>
<div class="amp-step" data-amp="twin" data-set="{&quot;volume&quot;:10}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Volume 10.</b> Even now it only starts to break up.</p></div>
```

Blackface 1963-67, AB763, 85 W into 4 ohm, four 6L6GC, solid-state rectifier, Normal and Vibrato channels, bright switch, spring reverb (Hammond / Accutronics), "vibrato" = tremolo by a neon + LDR bug; users incl. "Spring reverb." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_reverb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_reverb). Hammond's 1939 patent; Accutronics Type 4 / Type 8 units.

Yeh, David T., and Julius O. Smith. "Discretization of the '59 Fender Bassman Tone Stack." *Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Digital Audio Effects (DAFx-06)*, Montreal, 2006. [ccrma.stanford.edu/~dtyeh/papers/yeh06_dafx.pdf](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~dtyeh/papers/yeh06_dafx.pdf). Eqn. 1: the closed-form transfer function in the Treble / Middle / Bass pot positions, checked against SPICE in the paper; bilinear discretisation (2.3); Bassman values C1 250 pF, C2 = C3 20 nF, R1 250k, R2 1M, R3 25k, R4 56k.
